g3Statement: G3 for F1 holds with documented exceptions only: MU06/MU10 excluded from the denominator as EQUIVALENT-by-proof (conditional), MU11 OPEN (KILLABLE, E2), MU24 killed on component boundary only (reachable kill conditional on Q-MU06-01). No other mutant classification is changed.

mutants.label: And24.AndIn2 NOT in_False deactivated
conditions: GRP-1 (DOC): execution order GATE_001(119)->GATE_004(124)->GATE_005(125)->GATE_009(130)->GREEN.TonIn(135)->Symbol->And24(237), all pure AND in the same cycle; TON-2 (DOC 4.12.2): input 0 -> output 0 immediately, so GREEN(k)=1 implies in_False(k)=0.

GRP-2 (DERIVED, not DOC): a Symbol write is visible to a later-ordered reader in the same cycle and inputs are constant within a cycle. If the Symbol had inter-cycle delay, MU06 would be distinguishable (stale GREEN(k-1) with an in_False pulse). GRP-2 confirmation is assigned to the stand.
Topology of F1 as pinned above; any change of the GREEN chain or And24 voids the proof.
reevaluateWhen: GRP-2 confirmed or refuted by stand
Q-MU06-01 answered (role of in_False) if it changes And24/GREEN chain

mutants.label: RESET.OrIn1 b_Step_RnD_Set deactivated
conditions: Current Network3 topology: SafeResumption/MODE = Step1 OR RnD OR Step3 (exactly three active inputs); FBRs8(Step12).Reset = b_Step_RnD_Set; FBRs1/FBRs2 Reset contain b_Step12 (reset-dominant); FBRs3 Set only b_Step3_Set_3/b_Step3_Set_2; FBRs7(RnD) Set only b_Step_RnD_Set.
Network4/FBDecouple1 writes only Resets and b_Step1_Set/b_Step2_Set, both suppressed by reset-dominant b_Step12, so the proof does not depend on unknown Network4 values.
b_Step_RnD_Set(m) requires Step12 for the whole N11 TON delay => MODE(m)=0 => RESET.OrIn3 already resets the owner on the first Step12 scan; also MODE=0 in the reachable Step4 AND Step12 conflict.
reevaluateWhen: E2 status-assignment revision (review condition C4): MANDATORY re-evaluation, the proof relies on the current status assignment that E2 revises

mutants.label: RESET.OrIn2 b_Step4_Set deactivated
mutants.reason: Only observable effect: owner held 1 scan longer => DecOut1..4 fanout (STO reset, HV discharge, C2 reset; safe-direction outputs) 1 scan longer and the Step4 AND Step12 race window 1 scan wider. The distinguishing oracle (no Step4 AND Step12; loss of Healthy during accepted Run-down) is an E2 requirement not yet decided by the analyst; no honest F1 requirement test exists.
mutants.obligation: E2 test set must contain a requirement-based behavioral test that kills MU11 (review C3).

mutants.countsAsKilled: conditional (not counted as a reachable requirement kill)
mutants.reason: The killing GAP-HELD-ACROSS cases run on a fixture with b_Step3 held fixed. On the full program with real lifecycle (reviewer repro held-across-reach.mjs sha256 a6733ef0d70efb39d2db913ba474e565a38dcc30a1feef62964d2d2b5d7ad217, output held-across-reach.txt sha256 cf82a746c4220858b2cb0d781cedc1cd059cb2cc55f0fe4feb6593884dfe129f) loss of in_InterLock_NC_1/NC_2/in_LV_Connector_Interlock/in_Estop_PLC in Run immediately yields Step4, so the tester scenario is unreachable and F1 vs MU24 are indistinguishable there (RunDownAfterRepress false for both). The only reachable distinguisher found: in_False_SI2_CH8=TRUE pulse in Run (Run kept; F1: no down after re-press at 999 ms; MU24: down). Its expected reaction depends on open Q-MU06-01, so it is NOT adopted as a normative oracle.
assumptions: b_Step3 fixed by the fixture (test-injected internal state) in the original killers
